Simulate a longitudinal school health cohort

Source: R/sim-engine.R
wgh_simulate.Rd

wgh_simulate() generates a cohort of children followed through annual school health examinations. Each child's height curve is a SITAR-type transformation (size, timing and intensity) of a Preece-Baines mean curve, so every child's velocity is positive at every age. A latent adiposity score shifts timing, size and intensity, drives BMI through the WHO BMI-for-age reference and makes attendance informative. Children belong to latent phenotypes. The output separates what a real study would see (visits) from what only the simulation knows (truth_child, truth_visit).

Usage

wgh_simulate(
  n_children = 30000,
  preset = "wgh_like",
  seed = 2026,
  informative_visits = TRUE,
  style = c("book1", "book2"),
  monotone = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

n_children

Number of simulated children before enrolment rules are applied. About 60% of them appear in the visit data.

preset

A preset name or a settings list from wgh_preset().

seed

Random seed. The same seed always gives the same cohort.

informative_visits

If FALSE, attendance does not depend on adiposity.

style

Column names of the visit data: "book1" (pid, site, yearvisit, baz) or "book2" (schoolyear and bmiz as in Book 2).

monotone

Keep every child's measured heights non-decreasing with age, so the observed height velocity is never negative. Measurement error is added first, then each child's measured values are replaced by their isotonic regression (the closest non-decreasing sequence in the least-squares sense). Values change only where error created a decrease, where neighbouring visits are pooled to their mean, so observed increments of exactly zero occur. This slightly reduces the measurement error at those visits (see the validation tests). Use monotone = TRUE for teaching and for methods that assume non-negative observed velocity. Use FALSE to keep raw measurement error, as in real records, for example when studying methods that must cope with negative observed increments or when simulating false band moves. The true growth curves (height_true) are non-decreasing in both modes. If overrides in ... would make a true curve decrease, it is replaced by its running maximum, velocity_true is set to 0 where it is flat, and a warning says how many children were affected.

...

Settings that override single elements of the preset, for example beta_tempo_adiposity = c(Male = 0, Female = 0) for a world where adiposity does not affect timing.

Value

An object of class wgh_sim: a list with visits, roster, truth_child, truth_visit, pop_peaks, settings and call.

Details

Two presets are provided (see wgh_preset()):

  • "wgh_like" (default) resembles the published school health cohort: ages 18 months to 18 years, three sites of unequal size, early puberty (APHV near 12.2 years in boys and 9.2 years in girls) with a timing spread in girls about twice that in boys, high overweight and obesity in boys, falling obesity over calendar years and no examinations in 2021. Analyses run on it give tables and figures that resemble the papers. They do not reproduce published numbers, and they are not findings.

  • "reference" keeps the WHO-like settings of Book 2 Chapter 3, useful for teaching simulation and for known-truth exercises.

See also

wgh_preset(), wgh_add_messiness(), wgh_truth_check(), wgh_resemblance_report()

Examples

sim <- wgh_simulate(2000, seed = 1)
sim
#> <wgh_sim> preset "wgh_like", seed 1
#> 4077 visits from 1586 children (1980 enrolled)
#> Mean-curve APHV: boys 12.2 y, girls 9.2 y. PHV: 9.3 and 7 cm/y
#> Simulated data. Results resemble but do not reproduce published findings.
head(sim$visits)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 13
#>   pid     sex    site  dob        yearvisit examdate     age height weight   bmi
#>   <chr>   <fct>  <fct> <date>         <int> <date>     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>

#> 3 C000007 Female Site1 2020-06-15      2022 2022-12-17  2.50   90.4   13.7  16.8
#> 4 C000007 Female Site1 2020-06-15      2023 2023-09-30  3.29   97.3   16.5  17.4
#> 5 C000008 Female Site1 2017-04-06      2019 2019-11-16  2.61   92     14.6  17.2
